basis: Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; severe developmental disability, dystonia and ataxia affect 20/20 patients.
Lung agenesis, congenital cardiac defects and thumb malformations define the syndrome, despite lower reported frequencies for individual thumb findings.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures; strabismus affects 4/13 (~31%), supporting borderline ocular involvement. Feeding difficulties alone do not establish GI damage.
Tumor arises from cauda equina nerve roots; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-organ disease.
Benign tumor of the subglottic laryngeal airway.
Spherocytic hemolytic anemia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; intellectual disability/developmental delay occur in 80-99%. Retinal dystrophy is only 5-29%.
Locally infiltrating syringomatous adnexal tumor of nipple skin with sweat duct differentiation.
Intellectual disability and motor dysfunction define the syndrome. Broad vision abnormalities are nonspecific; explicit visual impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or oral-organ disease.
Severe developmental impairment, absent speech and epilepsy establish neurologic disease. Isolated skeletal and skin findings have very small assessed denominators.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle fatty replacement and distal amyotrophy each reported in 2/2 assessed patients, with distal leg weakness in 5/7. Small denominators limit certainty.
IRF6 spectrum predominantly affects oral development through lip pits and cleft lip/palate; popliteal skeletal abnormalities do not characterize most patients across the group.
Benign blood-vessel neoplasm located in the gingiva, an oral structure.
Structural myocardial disorder characterized by ventricular noncompaction, sometimes with ventricular dysfunction.
Inherited retinal cone-rod degeneration causing impaired acuity, color vision and central vision.
Defined fetal toxicity includes renal dysfunction and premature ductus closure, usually reversible. Respiratory insufficiency lacks established lung damage; cerebral/GI injuries are risks.
Progressive encephalopathy, amyotrophy and optic atrophy define the syndrome; amyotrophy occurs in 6/6 and optic atrophy in 2/6 patients.
Thyrotoxicosis and hypokalemia cause recurrent skeletal-muscle inexcitability and paralysis. Graves disease is an underlying cause, not an obligatory immune mechanism.
Classical complement-pathway immunodeficiency; associated infections and autoimmune diseases do not establish common direct damage to another organ across this umbrella.
Primary malignant bone tumor producing predominantly osteoid matrix.
Skeletal developmental disorder with skull underossification, short limbs, absent phalanges and syndactyly.
Noninvasive malignant epithelial neoplasm arising from the exocrine pancreas.
Congenital fusion of the temporomandibular joint. Feeding and breathing difficulties reflect restricted jaw opening without established additional organ damage.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis and Raynaud-associated vasculopathy define disease; esophageal dysfunction/reflux occurs in 30-79%. Pulmonary fibrosis and PAH are only 5-29%.
Auditory disorder defined by abnormally reduced sound tolerance and increased loudness sensitivity.
